target_customer: Biopharma developers building antibody drug conjugates and other protein therapeutics for solid tumors
problem: Conventional conjugation attaches linkers at random positions on antibodies. Catena couples two proteins at defined sites using an enzyme and native tyrosine and cysteine residues, enabling multi payload conjugates.
business_model: Therapeutics developer using its own protein conjugation platform; revenue not yet public
product_category: Protein conjugation platform and antibody drug conjugate therapeutics

founders.name: Marco Lobba
education: UC Berkeley, Ph.D., jointly in the labs of Matt Francis and Jennifer Doudna

founders.name: Matthew Francis
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page; Berkeley lab leader per search sources. No bio on the YC page.

founders.name: Geo Guillen
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by search summaries of Berkeley and Bakar Labs coverage; not on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Novel enzymatic protein coupling chemistry from Berkeley research, then developing therapeutics, requires deep biochemistry and long preclinical timelines.

defensibility.rationale: Chemistry is based on patented university research from the Francis and Doudna labs (patent inventors named in Berkeley IPIRA listing), hard to reproduce without the know how.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copy or purchase found in sources.

market_need_then: ADC makers sought site specific, multi payload conjugation; the company described random linker attachment as the traditional method (Berkeley and company materials).

branding.name_origin: Latin catena meaning chain, referencing linking proteins together (secondary profile, not a founder statement)
branding.domain_note: Company site redirects catenabiosciences.com to catenabio.com

rebrands.why: Short form now used on its domain; no source gives a reason or date

brand_strength.rationale: Meaningful name but no press on the brand itself; a biotech brand rests mostly on science.

pivots.to: Antibody drug conjugates for solid tumors
pivots.why: Reason not stated in sources found

outcome_analysis: Catena spun out of Berkeley protein chemistry research, joined YC in summer 2021, and raised a small seed extension in 2024, and added a chief business officer and chief scientific officer in January 2024. Capital raised appears modest for a therapeutics company, so progress depends on the planned Series A.
notes: The company site catenabio.com could not be fetched (domain check rate limited). The August 2021 seed lead is from Preqin only. Totals conflict across aggregators ($7.3M, $8.05M, $9.1M). Competitor list left empty: searches found no dated rivals near the 2021 batch (a Lonza article on tyrosine click chemistry is undated). Geo Guillen is listed as co-founder only via secondary summaries.
